answer:
Problem: Torsion of a cantilever solid circular shaft with two applied concentrated torques.
Model: Small-deformation, linear-elastic solid mechanics. Shaft is prismatic, solid circular cross-section, constant diameter. No body forces, no distributed loading, no axial or bending loads. Plane sections remain plane and undistorted (St. Venant torsion).
Geometry: Total shaft length L = 1200 mm. Diameter d = 30 mm, uniform along the full length. The shaft axis coincides with the x-axis.
Boundary condition: The left end at x = 0 is fixed (angle of twist θ(0) = 0, no rotation). The right end at x = L = 1200 mm is completely free (no rotational restraint, no reaction moment at x = L). Pure cantilever.
Applied loads (concentrated torques, sign convention: positive = counterclockwise when viewed looking in the +x direction): T₁ = +200000 N·mm applied at x = 1200 mm (free end). T₂ = -200000 N·mm applied at x = 400 mm (intermediate point). No other loads anywhere along the shaft.
Segments: The shaft is divided into two segments by the intermediate torque location. Segment A spans 0 ≤ x ≤ 400 mm. Segment B spans 400 mm ≤ x ≤ 1200 mm.
Material properties: AISI 1020 steel. Shear modulus G = 76923.1 MPa (N/mm²). Use this value exactly; do not round or substitute another value.
Units: All calculations use N, mm, and MPa consistently. Torques in N·mm, stresses in MPa, angles of twist in radians. No unit conversions are needed or permitted mid-calculation.
Internal torque determination: Compute the internal torque T_int(x) in each segment by making a free-body cut and enforcing equilibrium ΣMx = 0. Because the shaft is a cantilever fixed only at x = 0, the reaction moment at x = 0 equals the algebraic sum of the applied torques: M₀ = -(T₁ + T₂). Evaluate T_int in Segment B (400 to 1200 mm) first by cutting between x = 400 and x = 1200 and considering the portion from the cut to the free end. Then evaluate T_int in Segment A (0 to 400 mm) by cutting between x = 0 and x = 400 and considering the portion from the cut to the free end, which includes both T₂ and T₁.
Response quantities to report for each segment: The constant internal torque T_int (N·mm) and its sign. The polar moment of inertia J = π d⁴ / 32 (mm⁴) and the polar section modulus c/J = 32 / (π d³) (1/mm³). The maximum (outer-fiber) shear stress τ_max = |T_int| d / (2 J) (MPa) and its location on the cross-section (outer surface). The angle of twist at the free end θ(L) and at the intermediate point θ(400 mm), computed by summing θ = T_int L_seg / (G J) over each segment with proper signs. The total twist θ(L) relative to the fixed end.
Governing relations to state explicitly: T_int = internal torque from equilibrium. τ(r) = T_int r / J for 0 ≤ r ≤ d/2. τ_max = T_int (d/2) / J. θ = Σ (T_int,i · L_i) / (G · J) across all segments. J = π d⁴ / 32.
Deliverable: Present the internal torque diagram (values per segment), the shear stress values per segment, the twist at x = 400 mm and at x = 1200 mm, and a brief verification that equilibrium at x = 0 is satisfied. State any implicit assumptions made (e.g., torque applied exactly at the stated cross-section, no stress-concentration effects, Saint-Venant principle valid away from load application points).
